To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a low-noise and low-power front-end for the NEXT experiment that allows us to measure the energy of the electroluminiscence light with a precision better than 1%.

the NEXT-11 electronics is capable of achieving a 0.6% energy resolution for a 1 keV electron in a 2 mm drift gap, with an energy linearity better than 1.5%, and a 0.5% energy resolution for 5.9 keV X-rays, with a linearity better than ±0.5% for the full dynamic range.
we have designed a front-end electronics that allows the energy measurement of double-β decays with an accuracy better than 1%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a low noise front-end electronics to be used in the NEXT experiment, which is based on an innovative architecture.
the design, development and characterization of a custom-made front-end ASIC, the XENON-TPC-ASIC, for the NEXT experiment.
the design, construction and testing of a front-end electronics that is capable of detecting the weak scintillation light and the strong electroluminescense light produced in the gas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the front-end electronics developed and tested for NEXT-100 is a very robust, stable and reliable system that meets all the requirements of the NEXT experiment.
the NEXT front-end electronics fulfils the requirements for the NEXT experiment.
the front-end electronics for the NEXT experiment has been designed, built and tested, and is ready for installation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed, built and tested a front-end electronics that is able to cope with all the experimental conditions and requirements of NEXT.
we have developed a front-end electronics able to detect and measure the energy of the signals produced by the electroluminecence and primary scintillation.
the electronics design has been completed, the front-end electronics has been tested in a prototype TPC and the results show that it meets the requirements of the experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a front-end electronics based on a charge sensitive preamplifier and a shaper with 40 MHz sampling rate is capable of providing the required resolution for the NEXT experiment.
it is feasible to achieve energy resolution better than 0.5% FWHM at 2.5 MeV with this type of detector, and with a front-end electronics that can be easily implemented.
the design of a front-end electronics for a double beta decay detector can be optimized for the energy measurement and the primary scintillation signal detection.
